One of the best survival/crafting games I've played. With this type of game, at least in my experience, there seems to be a lot of jank, especially with combat. This game has great combat, in my opinion, and a pretty good questing system. The building system in this game is the best I've used. I also like the world being voxel. It just adds something to these games, for me anyway, when the terrain is deformable. I love it. 
I also enjoyed one of their other games, "Portal Knights", albeit a little more cartoony and cute than enshrouded, it is still a good experience. These devs make quality games and I will be keeping up with all of their future products.

Honestly, one of the most fun games i'm playing, over 100 hours and still barely touched the surface, gameplay is fun, building is incredibly satisfying to which i have spent allot of time doing only that.
100% recommend the game its also very beautiful.
I am truly excited to see what the future holds for this game or what comes next from Keen because another game like this and im sold.

Was hoping this could be a fun game for my friends and I to play together, but the forced shared progression really ruins it for us. We have disparate schedules and some folks prefer to spend more time crafting while others prefer to spend more time adventuring, but the current system punishes players unless they are all online at the same time AND keep their characters close to each other. If another character completes a quest and you weren't standing right next to them, you miss out on that and the corresponding experience. I've never played a multiplayer survival game so unaccommodating to parallel play and disparate gaming schedules. I haven't been able to play for a week now because one of my friends has been too busy and I don't want to ruin their quest progress. At this point it just makes more sense to turn off the server, uninstall the game, and find a game that will how and when we can play together.
I'm only 6 hours in and have just been building non-stop, quite addictive. A much better game than dragonwilds imo.

I love building system here, easy to start and to refine. You can quickly build a basic hut if you dont care about aesthetics, but if you care... you can spend endless hours refining your designs.
It's nice we can easily blend materials, modify small details, and build whatever form we like - be it a castle, tower, farm, mansion or village - its easy to make it pretty. And terrain adjustment! <3 Basements, tunnels, hills...

Dark Souls danger and gameplay with base building cozy survival craft AND its multiplayer co-op. YES PLEASE! 
Set out and explore the dangerous fallen world of Enshrouded. Fight, Survive, and Explore. Build a Village and rescue NPCs to live and work in it. Keen developers have worked hard to provide several big updates to add to the games content. The voxel based building in Enshrouded is the best of any game so far by a mile. The graphics are great, there are several biomes to explore, puzzles to solve, and tons of enemies to dispatch. Overall this game is a 10/10 when it comes to the Survival Craft genre. The best one out of the bunch.

Honestly, Enshrouded is such a great deal for its price. There's a ridiculous amount of content to enjoy, and you can easily sink dozens (if not hundreds) of hours into it without getting bored. There's always something to explore, craft, unlock, or work towards.

The base building is probably my favorite part. It's super fun, gives you tons of freedom, and you can get really creative with what you build. There's something really satisfying about starting with a simple little shelter and slowly turning it into a massive castle.

For what the game costs, you're getting so much bang for your buck. It's one of those games where you buy it thinking you'll play for a few hours and suddenly realize you've lost an entire weekend. Definitely recommend it.
Nice gameplay! Reminds a little of raft, LoZ TotK and Minecraft. The possibilities to build, explore and play with friends are immense and really motivating! :D

I don't write reviews. I'm writing one for this game because it's incredible. Even early access, the devs put so much thought into all possible aspects. It's hard to find any instances of a gotcha with beating the dev teams to an idea. It's dope a.f. 10/10

Been playing since almost day 1 and i gotta say this is one of the most fun and visually stunning games ive played in awhile! Either playing solo or with a couple of friends its always a good time! So much to explore and do and alot of cool user made worlds, If your big into Valhiem and those style games this should definately scratch that itch and more!

Honestly not sure what they did or how they managed it, but the game has the graphical quality of pong now. It was not this atrocious when I first played. Changed settings between quality and performance and had zero changes in looks? Tried changing resolution as well and no effect there either. Not a clue in the slightest why it looks like this.
Rather not recommend a game that looks like I'm looking through a pixelated stained-glass church window. 
Won't even say anything on gameplay because I last played months ago, and I quit when I couldn't fix the graphical problems. note: same platform I played originally.

buy in sale
I enjoy this game a lot. That being said, the platforming is fucking awful. The rage I've felt playing this game has no equal. Elden Ring was less infuriating.
Prime example of what an early access game should be. At this point it's way better than most fully released survival games. Very fun!

I normally don't buy early access games especially with a steep price point of $39.99 for a n unfinished game, but I took a chance on a friends's recommendation.

This is more of an first impression review so keep that in mind. I really wanted to like it, but I couldn't get behind the artstyle especially with the weird proportions of your character. Felt weird to me and I couldn't find any lorr reason for it while playing. The exploring at least in the early game wasn't that rewarding. My friend's and I would do a dungeon area just to be rewarded with almost nothing. Melee combat seems much more fun than magic as well. Magic really needs a better basic attack with the wands. You shoot one flaccid spark that barely does anything. There are spells and I hope there are more, but early game it just wasn't fun playing that style of gameplay.

The base building mechanics seem alright with what we had available playing.

I'm not the biggest fan of the genre, although I have loved some in the past like valheim, but this one for asking the price and early access it just isn't worth it. Wait until full release. I may come back then and play with my friends and see if opinion changes on full release, but judging for what it is now and unless you are a big fan of this genre I'd wait.

Never had a game with base building like this, blended with the incredible graphics, top tier combat and levelling i could not recommend this enough, not that ive ever recommended a game before but this one deserves it

Game is enjoyable through and through. There's something for everyone, whether it be exploration, (shiny new/reworked) combat, questing, or base building. This game really shines in the freedom it gives you to do what you will with your world. It's easily become one of my favorite creative games to do big projects on (check some of them out on my Steam profile). The dev team has also done a fantastic job of consistently pushing out high quality content, as well as adhering (and exceeding) to their released roadmap. Genuinely the best building game on Steam, in my opinion. Runs great on my mid PC on mostly high settings, and looks gorgeous.
Exceptionally fun. Not fully fleshed out yet, but great either way. Best spent in co-op when tasks can be split a little, otherwise it could become a chore for some resources.

The enemy spam as you progress though the game makes the solo experience unbearable. Fighting a boss while 10 randoms enemies interrupt everything you try to do is not fun. Crafting gear seems pointless since the best gear is the legendary stuff you find (RNG made it so I got none for my build).

Best survival crafting game I played this year. I also enjoyed that it lets you do puzzles, and or complete areas in your own way instead of making you take the path they made you to follow.

out of lockpicks, break down the wall, can't figure out the puzzle, just mine under the door.

Come to place from the wrong size, bunny hop the mountain or access it from spire and glider.

Resource gathering is not really much of a burden either, unless you totally forget where to get certain items.
Best Survival Game I've ever played. Skill tree makes it really fun and finding new areas is always exciting.

If you want good building this is the game! I'd like to see some weather however as it's always bright. Just some rain would definitely make it perfect.

Weather added, guess it's just perfect now.

Hi its safe to say that I love this game after playing almost 2000 hours. I love the freedom that game give to let my creativity run wild. I recommend it to any one who want to create and challenge themselves

The game has been stable for the last 60h of gameplay, so I'm switching my negative review to a positive one. Originally, I had issues with the game crashing shortly after loading. I updated drivers and verified game files. That seems to have fixed it.

The Miasma looks scary at first, but quickly turns into background fog. Combat and exploration are solid, but let’s be honest: the real magic is in the building system. It’s intuitive, detailed, and ridiculously satisfying - we spent hours crafting bases that would make medieval architects cry with joy.

Pros:

Phenomenal building system - one of the best in the genre
Exploration is fun and rewarding
Great co-op experience

Cons:

The Miasma goes from spooky threat to mild inconvenience pretty fast
Once you know what you’re doing, the challenge drops off noticeably
Our biggest enemy wasn’t the fog - it was storage management

If you like building, looting, and yelling “Who messed up the loot sorting again?!” at your friends, you'll love Enshrouded. Even more so in co-op. And if not.. just build yourself a castle out of spite. It'll be beautiful.

Great game, definitely one of my favorites. Easily one of the best games ever made. Can't wait to see the future of this game. Hopefully this game keeps getting great updates and some story like dlcs in the future.

Keep up the great work devs!

One of the best games out there, so much to do. Great building and an amazing world/ Lore built world! 
Love it!!! Can't wait for future updates!!

Wow, just Wow!
I have not had a game draw me in like this in ages. 500+ hours, 100% Achievements and I can't stop playing. Fantastic controls, Beautiful graphics, Excellent Survival and Build mechanics, pretty good Skill tree with compelling character builds. The Accessibility controls that make it so you can play the game the way you want to play. All of it... Chefs Kiss! Every early access patch release has made the game better and 1.0 is only a few weeks away. If you haven't purchased this game yet you are missing out.
I Can't Wait!!!

Really enjoy playing the game! Graphics are awesome and do not require RTX 4090 to enjoy in the beauty of it like ASA does ;) . Very playable game, lots of room for adding new features and biomes , probably even different bosses. Highly recommended!
cant believe game is in early access with so much content....240 hrs on the clock...money well spent.

Game is great so far. Ignore the bad reviews because they are complaining about multiplayer server issues and that is all. It's a new popular game made by a small studio. They have already said that a hotfix is coming ASAP to remedy the server issues. The game itself is great. I have been itching for more ever since the demo.

I am hooked. The game works great and doesn't crash like it did last year for me. A few updates and I am at it exploring and destroying my enemies. I liken this game to Dark souls meets minecraft. I have increased the difficulty and I still die from time to time, but it is challenging and enjoyable. I recommend.

2026 and we still got games that are single-core CPU bound, I should not be getting sub-60 FPS with this setup on high settings 1440p with 18% CPU usage and 50% GPU usage, you made a custom game engine specifically for this project but couldn't bother optimizing it for multi-core processing? why not just use literally any other engine on the market at that point? I shouldn't need fake AI frames and DLSS just to get your game to run properly on a high-end system, it's a shame because this truly is a good game but I simply can not recommend it to anyone who doesn't have bleeding-edge hardware that can brute force through the horrible optimization issues.
Such a fun game so far, highly recommend. Especially since it's on sale as of right now!
This game has taken hours of my life away as soon as I launch it. THIS GAME is absolutely stunning and I cannot wait until full release. If you are on the fence about purchasing, just do it.

The keybinding options for this game make no sense and some are tied to building and combat for no reason. If you change one in building, it changes your combat buttons as well. I have played games with much more complex interactions that do this with ease but in 2026 Enshrouded can't figure it out.

Edit: After a ridiculous amount of time, I managed to remap the buttons to a playable state. It required remapping almost every single build hotkey to have something more intuitive and in line with most other survival games. It should not require that level of remapping to change a few keys for combat. Combat keys and build keys should not be linked and this problem would be solved. (This pertains to hotkeys for controller, I don't know if the same issue exists for M&K)

In it's current state of early access, it is a great builder, but lacks depth and life in most other areas.

The content doesn't feel enough yet inbetween areas. I'm constantly under leveled, and the quests either don't give enough XP, or aren't exciting enough to grind out (aside from the key quests that unlock items and options). As an extension of this, fast traveling to a tower and gliding across ravines to collect the items I just lost to monsters twice my level isn't very exciting on the third repeat.
But as initially mentioned, it's a great builder and very chill when it comes to that side of the game, assuming you've unlocked all the options for building, I'm optimistic that the game will improve with the foundations it's building upon.

Actually pretty awesome. I've played alot of these survival games but Enshrouded finds a great balance between all the good of the other games and adds more depth in other ways. 

Wish this was an MMO! lol Really enjoying playing this with my GF right now.

There's so much to do in this game, and the building system is amazing! I've been having a blast exploring the world, gathering resources, and bringing everything back home to craft new stuff.

As a mage/healer, though, I really wish we could assign skills directly to the action bar. Having to constantly scroll up and down in the middle of combat just to find the skill I need is super annoying. Food, potions, and a few other items could definitely use bigger stack sizes, too.

And my biggest gripe? The character designs and outfits. I'm sorry, but everything looks absolutely hideous, feels like they don't even fit in the game that looks so beautiful. I'm at the point where I'm practically begging for a mod so I can fix the looks myself.

Other than that, I'm really enjoying the game!

Been duo for 45 hours at this point, and this game shows so much promise. I've been in awe since the moment I started playing all the way until now and it's been an absolute blast of a game. The amount of stuff to do.. the difficulty of the enemies. The RPG elements. This could EASILY be a soft MMO with a 100-person server for progression. I love this game. I'm so excited to see what else these devs can make. Thank you for making such an amazing game. I highly recommend this to anyone since you'll 100% get your money's worth.

Top tier + W content

But its really in a bad need for optimization .. for such a game with simple art styles .. shaders should have never taken that long neither FPS drops that bad when encountering large bases and builds

Even as an early access game, this has HOURS of entertaining game play and an unfinished map with SO MANY land marks to find. A lot of them ARE the same, flame shrines, and obelisks, but that doesn't diminish the joy of finding them. 
I keep looking forward to finding the next building block and what that'll look like, and what the next area will be, and knowing that there's still so much to do - I'm excited for the full release.
It is better than Minecraft, some of the respawns suck. I think of the game like a multi tool, it could be better in a lot of ways, however it has a lot of functions.

I want to recommend this game badly. It's my favorite survival/multiplayer game. But the compiling shaders made it that one of my friends quit, he got through it twice, but the third time: a small patch after a bigger path, was just too much. He has a decently good laptop but the compiling shaders take up to hours, which isn't even a guarantee cause it can still crash. I really hope they'll end up fixing this.
I think what these devs have made here is a great game, it is huge, has tons of content and plays on my pc like a dream. How many games can you say that about?

absolutely atrocious to get to run decently for some reason and even then you can have random issues cropping up from time to time, but a seemingly endless sea of content and exploration with kinda souls-like combat... unless you encounter a group of the one handed sword guys then its a war of attrition against constant bullshit running attacks that do far too much damage that they can just take turns spamming forever apparently

A bit of adventuring, a bit of tending to your garden. Oh, we're building a fort now. Now we need copper so back to adventuring. Stop! I need to befreind a cat! Oh some dungeons to explore, need to do that to level a bit.

This game is a bit of everything i a lovely little mix that lets the hours go past with friends. Does it have problems? Yes. Could every game system be better and less clunky? yes. Do I still love it? Absolutetely!

So much to this game and rewarding on many levels, you want a game that you can sink into, build at a level no other game offers or skill tree that is fun and diverse enough to offer unique builds, this is your game.
Just a few little things to left to perfect, but this game is really a gem. Valheim + Breath of the Wild. Unreal quality for the price.

minecraft meets elder scroll with great graphics and gameplay. whether you wanna go crazy building a castle or just explore the world and kill stuff, you can find it in this game. Really enjoy it, i hope they keep improving it. I play solo but if you have friends they can go along in your world and help you kick some a**.
